walkthroughs.body_html:
QC = end-of-line inspection. QA = quality built in.

QA prevents defects (training, standard procedures); QC catches them. QA is cheaper long-term.

Lean cuts every kind of waste: time, materials, motion, defects, over-production.

Common techniques: JIT, continuous improvement (Kaizen), and cell production.

JIT: stock arrives just as needed. Low storage costs but vulnerable to supplier delays.

JIC: keep a buffer. Safer but ties up cash in inventory and risks waste.

mcqs.q: What is Taylor's theory of scientific management?
options: Workers are motivated primarily by money; efficiency is maximised by breaking tasks into standardised steps, training workers in 'the one best way', and using piece-rate pay.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.
Taylor said workers are motivated by recognition and teamwork.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Taylor invented the assembly line at Ford.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
